name: Hermon
overview: Mount Hermon is a significant geographical landmark in the northern region of ancient Palestine, prominently mentioned as a boundary of the land taken from the Amorite kings by Israel (Deuteronomy 3:8, Joshua 12:1). Scripture reveals that this mountain was known by different names among neighboring peoples: the Sidonians called it Sirion, the Amorites named it Shenir, and it is also referred to as Sion (Deuteronomy 3:9, 4:48). Hermon’s presence in the biblical narrative highlights its strategic and cultural importance, situated near the land of Mizpeh and extending into the valley of Lebanon (Joshua 11:3, 11:17).
